_note: Boxes are NORMALISED to the tile (0-1). ALMOST PURE ROCK -- this is the distant-summit band and roughly 90% of the pixels are stone. There is no canopy here and nothing that resembles the foreground leaf walls of the lower scroll. The whole middle of the tile is one enormous pale summit face, drawn with long wandering parallel 牛毛皴 hemp-fibre strokes and almost no wash; a second cliff runs diagonally down the right side. Real foliage exists in exactly four places, all of it small and all of it TREE-SHAPED (a visible dark vertical trunk stroke with a flat tufted crown sitting on it, repeated along a line): (1) a tree line following the crest that climbs from x~0.36,y~0.28 up to x~0.62,y~0.02 in the upper centre; (2) a much clearer tree line on the right-hand ridge, a loose group of flat-crowned trees at x 0.62-0.81, y 0.30-0.47 with a pale blue wash laid behind them, continuing up-right as a thinner file to the top right corner; (3) the crown of a large near tree clipped by the BOTTOM edge at x 0.44-0.79 -- the only blue-green 夾葉 leaf colour in the tile, hung on a clearly drawn ochre trunk that forks at y~0.93; (4) a small clump of layered pines clipped by the BOTTOM-LEFT corner. Everything else that reads dark is stone, and this tile is full of the exact decoy that made the rock sway on the previous pass. Four named decoys: (a) the RIGHT CLIFF below y 0.45 -- x 0.62-1.0 is covered in dense 点苔 moss dabs that at thumbnail size look identical to the tree line 0.2 above them; magnified there is not one trunk in it, the dabs sit flat on the stone and follow the rock contours rather than standing upright; (b) the dark ink ridge across the top centre-right (x 0.55-0.80, y 0.00-0.14), a shadowed crest wash plus moss, no tree glyphs; (c) the hemp-fibre fans on the left spur and lower right, long parallel lines splaying downhill that mimic pine needles; (d) the BLUE WASH at the far left top (x 0.00-0.14, y 0.03-0.22) is a distant mountain silhouette in blue pigment, not vegetation -- any colour-based foliage detector will grab it first. One genuine but sub-floor object is deliberately omitted: a single bare sapling in fine dark line at about x 0.51-0.56, y 0.55-0.63, standing on the summit face; it has no leaf mass and is under the size floor, so it must not be animated.

objects.name: group of flat-crowned trees on the right ridge
objects.note: the best-defined foliage in the tile: eight or ten small trees standing along a ridge shoulder, each with a dark vertical trunk stroke and a horizontally spreading dotted crown, with a pale blue wash brushed in behind them to push the ridge back. Box includes the pale silk between the crowns, so a mask must key on the dark dot clusters; the ridge rock under their feet at the bottom of the box must not move

objects.name: thin file of trees climbing the right ridge to the top corner
objects.note: SEARCH REGION -- the trees run as a narrow DIAGONAL line from lower-left to upper-right inside this box, so well over half the box is bare cliff. Same glyph as ridge-trees-right-lower but smaller and sparser. Continues into t007. Do not fill this box

objects.name: trees on the upper-centre crest, lower half
objects.note: SEARCH REGION. Small dark tufts strung along the silhouette edge of a ridge that climbs to the right; the tufts sit ON the crest line, so the lower-right half of the box is the rock body of that ridge. Trunks are one or two pixels wide at this scale -- these read as trees only because the tufts stand clear of the ridge outline against pale silk

objects.name: trees on the upper-centre crest, upper half
objects.note: SEARCH REGION, continues crest-trees-centre-lower up to the top edge where it is clipped. The right end of this box runs into the dark shadowed ridge (rock-ridge-dark-top) and that overlap is rock, not leaves

objects.name: crown of a large tree clipped by the bottom edge
objects.note: the ONLY blue-green leaf colour in the tile: rounded outlined leaf clusters washed pale blue-green, on an ochre trunk that forks low. This is the top of a much larger foreground tree that lives in the tiles below (band y>4136); only its head is in this tile. The bare twiggy branches reaching up to y~0.86 at x 0.47-0.55 carry no leaves and belong to trunk-bottom-centre

objects.name: ochre trunk and bare branches of the bottom-edge tree
objects.note: warm ochre wood with dark contour, forking into bare upward twigs above the leaf mass. RIGID -- the leaves should pivot about this, it must not translate

objects.name: clump of small pines at the bottom-left corner
objects.note: four or five layered dark pines with clearly visible straight trunks, clipped by both the left and bottom edges. Pure ink, no colour wash, which is why a colour-keyed pass misses them entirely -- the opposite error to the moss-dot decoys. At the size floor; treat any sway as very small

objects.name: the great pale summit face, centre
objects.note: the dominant object in the tile: a single vast rounded rock mass built from long parallel hemp-fibre strokes with sparse moss along its folds. NEVER animate. The lone bare sapling near x 0.53, y 0.59 stands on this face and is below the size floor

objects.name: right-hand cliff below the tree line
objects.note: THE PRINCIPAL DECOY OF THIS TILE. Dense 点苔 moss dabs in ragged vertical chains over hemp-fibre strokes; at thumbnail size this is indistinguishable from the genuine tree line just above it. The test that separates them: these dabs have no trunk under them and their chains follow the rock's fold lines downhill instead of standing vertical on a ledge. This is the family of surface that got the earlier automatic pass rejected -- if this box moves, the rock moves

objects.name: dark shadowed ridge across the top centre-right
objects.note: DECOY. The darkest passage in the upper tile -- a wet grey wash on the shaded side of a crest, dotted with moss. Reads as a tree mass at a glance; no repeated tree glyph anywhere in it. Clipped by the top edge

objects.name: vertical rock spur down the left third
objects.note: a tall ridge running the height of the tile, its left silhouette picked out with moss dabs. Those edge dabs are the same decoy as rock-cliff-right, on a smaller scale

objects.name: rock shelves down the lower left
objects.note: pale stepped ledges in hemp-fibre stroke, continuing down to the pines in the corner. Rigid

objects.name: blue-washed distant peak, top left
objects.note: DECOY FOR COLOUR MASKS. A far mountain laid in flat blue-green pigment with a soft top edge -- the same pigment family as the leaf wash on the bottom-edge tree, and the largest patch of non-grey colour in the tile. It is stone. Continues into t005
